period: Track record from ECMWF AIFS ENS 00 UTC runs of 13 May to 5 November 2026, checked against NASA IMERG Late V07C for 14 May to 10 November 2026. 177 runs over six months, most of them monsoon, so it says little about winter.
wording: agreed with the satellite estimate, never correct (SPEC 5.9)
note_small_reference_groups: Some reference groups are small -- a square in November has only six to ten days behind it -- and a small group's own average fits its own days closely, which makes it harder to beat. Where that happens our skill is if anything understated.
crps_note: CRPS is on the ensemble of daily totals, not on the thresholded events, so it has no threshold. Its baseline is the observed daily totals at that square over the 30 days ending the day before the run, which is out of sample -- unlike the Brier reference of 5.3, which is not. The two are never to be compared as if they were the same yardstick.

not_computed.corp: The CORP isotonic diagnostic (SPEC 5.7) has not been computed. Nothing on the site may mention it.
not_computed.random_error: The high-randomError sensitivity (SPEC 5.7) has not been computed. Nothing on the site may mention it.

meta.spec_sha256_note: over SPEC.md with CRLF normalised to LF, which are the committed bytes

variants.name: inland51
variants.note: all 51 members, coastal squares left out (SPEC 5.11 rule 6)

bootstrap.reference: fixed, computed once from the full sample (SPEC 5.5)

reference.key: square x calendar month of the forecast day x lead day x threshold

crps.baseline: the observed daily totals at that square over the 30 days ending the day before the run
crps.forms: plain and fair; the fair form corrects for ensemble size, so it is the one the skill score uses and the one the 51-against-50 comparison can be read from
